learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and application of the principles of strength of materials.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to organize and plan time.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.

Students should be able to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences usually demonstrated by developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.
Students will have learned to systematically solve problems and questions related to the subject, enabling them to relate concepts and develop criteria for analyzing the solutions obtained.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Methods of strength of materials. Real system and calculation scheme. External and internal forces. Displacements, deformations, and stresses. Hooke's Law. Principle of superposition. Isostatic and hyperstatic systems. Tensile and compression test. Diagram. Essential mechanical properties of the material. Safety factor.

Tension and compression: Internal forces and stresses developed in the cross-sections of a bar under tension and compression. Displacements and deformations in tension. Statically determined (isostatic) and statically indeterminate (hyperstatic) systems. Normal force diagram. Hyperstatic cases in tension. Thermal expansion.
Geometric characteristics of cross-sections: Static moments of the section. Moments of inertia of the section. Principal axes and principal moments of inertia.

Bending (I): Internal forces occurring in the cross-sections of bars under bending. Bending moment, normal force, and shear force diagrams. Diagrams for point load, uniformly distributed load, and point bending moment cases.

Bending (II): Stresses in the case of transverse bending. Displacements in bending. General equation of the elastic curve. Solution by integration of simple problems. Transverse bending. Shear stresses in composite beams.
Torsion: Shear strain and shear stress. Displacements, deformations, and stresses in the torsion of solid and hollow cylindrical bars. Torsional moment diagram.
Equilibrium bifurcation in column compression: Buckling. Euler's equation. Critical load. Dependence of critical load on boundary conditions.

Theory of limit states or component failures: Stress state at a point. Relationship between stresses and deformations in 3D problems. Principal stresses. Principal stresses in the plane problem. Rotation of stresses in the plane. Elastic strain energy. Strain energy due to shape change. Von Mises equivalent stress.
Practical 1. Verification of a planar bar structure
Practical 2. Obtaining elastic moduli of beams of different profiles and materials by measuring displacements under known loads
Practical 3. Measurement of transverse displacements in beams. Theoretical verification
Practical 4. Experimental measurement of Euler's critical buckling load
teaching_methods: Solving problems applied to real situations
Individual work (reading and understanding guides and complementary material, completing pre-activities, and peer assessment)
Collaborative laboratory work (taking measurements, calculations, completing reports/group work)
assessment_rules: Assessment occurs via Continuous Evaluation or Single Evaluation. For Continuous Evaluation, the final grade comprises four development tests (A: 5%, B: 20%, C: 10%, D: 50%) and laboratory activities (15%), each requiring specific minimum scores; only Test D and lab components are recoverable in resits. For Single Evaluation, the grade is based on a comprehensive development test (85%) divided into three blocks and laboratory activities (15%), all requiring a minimum of 5/10. Failure to meet minimums in any component or demonstrate fundamental understanding results in failure, with specific grade floors for different conditions.
